title: Field-Level Event Splintering (Micro-Events)
pattern: Emitting individual fine-grained events for every mutated field instead of a cohesive semantic event for the overall business action.
why_bad: Floods the event store and message broker with thousands of micro-events. Subscribers cannot validate domain invariants across fields easily because the data arrives splintered in separate event handlers. It also forces high coupling to specific structural fields instead of business intents.
detection: Event structures containing only a single mutated attribute field coupled with a surrogate identifier, where multiple such events are emitted concurrently during a single domain command.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Low-level reactive audit systems that explicitly track keystrokes or precise, individual cell edits in collaborative sheets.
fix:
Consolidate related attribute updates into a single cohesive, semantic domain event representing the business intention.
```rust
struct UserContactDetailsChanged {
    id: u64,
    first_name: String,
    last_name: String,
    email: String,
}
```
source: *Vaughn Vernon - Implementing Domain-Driven Design (2013)*, Chapter 8, "Domain Events" and Chapter 10, "Aggregates" (Refactoring large events, p. 302).
